texts: doha about this world being a short fair that we just visit, with a fish and a bridge
We crossed the old bridge to the village fair as kids and watched fish being sold; now I am old and the whole fair seems to have packed up while I looked away
Write a doha about the world as a fair that opens for a few days, where the fish is sold and a bridge carries the crowd across, and then everyone packs up and goes their way
fish, bridge, passing fair
The bridge brims with fairgoers and the fish glitters in the tents of a festival that closes at dusk, as the world does
I told my grandfather I had finally bought a flat, and he laughed and said, so did I, once, and the boat that brought me to this city was supposed to be temporary
Please write a doha where a boat carries the guests to a fair on an island, where they stay a few days and then sail back, as a picture of how we all just visit this world briefly
The boat brings the visitors to a fair of lights and music, and the same boat takes them home when the drums are silent
boat, world's brief fair
doha with a boat about how the world is just a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha in which a bier and a boat both wait at the edge of the fair, since everyone who comes to this world as a guest for a few days must be carried away, whatever they bought
doha with a bier and a boat, the world is a fair and we go home soon
bier, boat, passing fair
The fair is loud, the bier is silent, and the boat at the edge of the water takes every guest away
My cousin was at the village fair on Sunday, laughing on the boat ride, and on Friday they carried him on a bier; the fair is still running but he is not there
doha about the world being a fair we visit for few days
A festival of colours and voices that is taken down before the week is out: so is the world to those who linger
Please write a doha in the manner of Kabir that says this world is just a fair visited for a few days, that guests who stay too long misunderstand it for their home, and that all must leave
I overheard two old men at a wedding saying that the good thing about life is that you are only here for the festival, and that stuck with me
world is a fair
The drums of the fair are loud in the evening and the ground is bare by morning, and the guests have moved on
Kabir often said that the world is a gathering of a few days, where each takes his tent for a short while and leaves, so write me a doha in simple words about this fair
The fair came to our town last week and left yesterday, and the empty field made my mother say that is what life is, a short visit; I want a doha in this spirit
world's passing fair
doha about how the world is a short fair and we all pack up soon
My landlord keeps telling me this flat is mine for now, and I think of how everyone is a tenant on this earth; the bier at the neighbour's place last week reminded me
bier, world is a fair
Write a doha in which a bier is carried out of a crowded fair, and the guests only pause for a moment before they go back to buying and selling, forgetting that their own stay is also short
doha with a bier in it, about the world being just a fair for a few days
The bier goes out through the gate of the fair, and the fair goes on, forgetting that it is also a guest
A cloud passed over the fairground and the whole thing was packed away before night, and my uncle, who has sung with a loud tongue at fairs, said that is life
Write a doha about a cloud over a fair and a tongue that praises the day, and how every guest finds the festival over before he has finished enjoying it, so he should not call it home
A cloud crosses the fair, a tongue sings its praise, and both are gone by evening, as is the whole gathering
cloud, tongue, passing fair
doha with a cloud and a tongue about the world being a fair we just visit
My grandmother kept a parrot and wore a forehead mark every day, and she said that she had attended the fair of life long enough to know the closing time
parrot, forehead mark, brief fair
doha with a parrot and a forehead mark, the world is a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha where a parrot repeats the cries of a fair, and a woman with a forehead mark buys her trinkets, though both will leave when the drums fall silent and the field is bare
The parrot learns the fair's cries and the forehead mark shines, but by dusk the ground is empty
cremation ground, passing fair
The fair of the living ends at the cremation ground, where all guests are counted out and none are left
Write a Kabir-style doha about the cremation ground at the far edge of the great fair of the world, where each guest finally arrives after buying and selling, and from which nobody returns
doha about a cremation ground and how the world is just a fair
When we left the fair I noticed the cremation ground behind the field, and I realised that every one of us is only visiting the world; I want a doha on this
I checked into an inn for just one night in a city I've loved all my life, and I realised we live in this world the same way, guests with a short booking
doha about the world being an inn where we stay a few days
Please write a doha in which the world is an inn where travelers stop for the night, and in the morning they must pay the bill and go, though some foolishly mistake it for their own home
The inn is full of laughter tonight and will be bare tomorrow, and all the guests have somewhere else to go
inn, world's brief stay
Salt goes into every dish at the fair and is gone from the plate by night, as is the guest who tasted it
At the village fair my grandfather would always buy salt and said that is all he needed from it; he lived as a guest on this earth and died as one
salt, world is a fair
Write a doha where salt is sold at a short-lived fair and every buyer carries a little away, saying this world is only a visit of a few days and must not be mistaken for a permanent home
doha with salt in it, the world is a fair and we dont stay
Please write a doha in which a fly lands on a skeleton at the closing of the fair, and the verse says that the guests who thought the festival would last forever have gone, leaving the empty tents
fly, skeleton, passing fair
At the end of the fair a fly sat on the skeleton of a dead goat behind the tents, and the old man beside me said, that is how long it all lasts; I want a doha about this
The fly circles the skeleton at the end of the fair, where the revelry has ended and only the dust remains
doha with a fly and a skeleton, the world is just a fair and we pass through
The lamps are lit for a few evenings, the music plays, the crowd thins, and the world is a fair that pulls up its tents
doha about the world being a fair, we only visit
The tents are already coming down at the end of the festival, and my father said look, that is how we will all go, one tent after another
Write a Kabir-style doha in which the world is likened to a fair that stays only for a few days, when each person tastes a few sweets and leaves, and none can claim the ground as his own
fair, brief visit
There was a cuckoo singing near the furnace at the fair, and my grandfather said all of it was only on loan for a few days; the cuckoo and the furnace and all of us
cuckoo, furnace, passing fair
doha with a cuckoo and a furnace, the world is a short fair
Write a doha in which a cuckoo sings near a roaring furnace in the middle of the fair, though both will be gone when the festival ends, and the guests will find nothing but empty ground
The cuckoo sings above the furnace in the fair, and both fall silent when the evening comes to pack up the tents
doha about the world being a fair that we visit only for a few days
My niece looked at the balloons at the fair and asked, where do they go after, and I said to the same place we all go; I want a doha on that
The fair has its balloons and music, and the hours rush, and nobody asks where the hours go
Please write a doha in the voice of Kabir which says that the world is a fair of a few days, in which we come to look around and buy a few things and then go home empty
world is a fair
door, passing fair
There is a door at the end of the fair through which each guest must go, and it opens in only one direction
Write a doha where the fair has one door through which everyone enters and another through which everyone leaves, so no one mistakes the temporary festival for his own permanent dwelling
doha with a door in it about the world being just a short fair
The doors of the fair opened this morning and will close this evening, and I thought of how we all come in through one door and leave through another
When I visit my childhood town now, I see strangers living in the rooms where my family laughed, and I think: we were all only passing through, and the town goes on without us
doha about how everyone is just visiting this world
The fair fills the field with lanterns and noise, and the next morning finds it bare and swept
world, brief visit
Write a doha in Kabir's manner saying the world is a fair for a few days, that people come with families and sell and buy and quarrel, and then they leave, and the field is empty again
A house for the night, and by morning another guest sleeps in the bed where you slept, for the world is a fair
Write a doha in which the world is a fair and the house on the fairground is only rented for a few days, so that those who paint its walls and plant gardens are foolish, as the lease is short
house, world is a fair
We rented a house near the fair for the festival week and by the end we had become so attached to it that leaving was difficult; that is also what life feels like
doha with a house and the world being just a short fair
I spent a lifetime searching for a philosopher's stone at festivals and fairs, and at the end I understood that the whole world is a visit that ends
The philosopher's stone is sold at every fair and bought by every fool, who leaves with an empty pocket and a full heart
philosopher's stone, world's fair
doha with a philosopher's stone, the world is a fair and we leave soon
Write a doha in which a seller at a passing fair claims to have the philosopher's stone, and the guests who buy it find at the closing that the fair, the seller and their own stay were all temporary
Write a doha in which a snake glides through the grass at the edge of the fair, while the guests laugh and buy, forgetting that the festival is brief and that they too will slip away at nightfall
snake, world is a fair
The snake sleeps under the fairground boards, and the fair above it has only a few more days to dance
The snake charmer at the fair said his act is only for three days and then he moves on; I told him that is also how we live on earth
doha with a snake, the world is a fair, we only visit
Please write a doha about a tongue that praises the world at the fair and a thorn that pricks the foot of the one who forgets he is a guest, so that we remember this stay is only brief
doha with a tongue and a thorn, the world is a fair and we are guests
My mother says what you say with your tongue at a fair is forgotten, and the thorn in your foot is the only thing you remember; both belong to a few brief days
tongue, thorn, passing fair
The tongue sings the praise of the fair and the thorn reminds the foot that the road is long and the fair is short
My grandfather's shadow still falls on the lion statue at the fair ground where he worked, though the fair only comes for a week a year; he used to say we are all visitors
doha about a shadow and a lion, the world is a fair we visit briefly
The lion roars in the fair, the shadow grows long, and by evening the whole show has gone
shadow, lion, passing fair
Write a doha in which the shadow of a lion falls across the fair at sunset, and the guests, proud as lions, see that their stay is short and that they must leave their places to others
doha with a rope and a boat, the world is a fair, we visit and go
rope, boat, passing fair
At the fair, a boat was tied with a rope to the pier and everyone rode it for a few coins and left; I thought, that's us
Please write a doha in which a boat tied with a rope waits for fairgoers, and the rope is untied at dusk and the boat leaves with the last guests, for nobody may stay beyond the fair's closing
The rope that held the boat at the fair is let go at dusk, and the guests are carried away
The rainbird sings for the first drops over the fair and the date palm sways above, and a few days later the field is bare
Write a doha in which a rainbird cries from a date palm at a fair that will end in a few days, so that those who hear it remember that they are only guests in this world
rainbird, date palm, passing fair
doha with a rainbird and a date palm, the world is a fair we leave soon
A rainbird was calling from the date palm all through the village fair and my aunt said it is calling us to remember the fair is short
fair's closing hour
The man who sold sweets at the festival told me he sets up in a new town every week, and I told him that is how we all live; I want a doha about that
doha about us all being visitors in this world
The fair rolls out its carpets and rolls them up again, and nobody has yet found the owner of the ground
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying that this world is the fair of a few days, in which we have gathered and played and will soon pack up, so no one should quarrel over the little ground we use
doha about the world being a fair and we leave when it ends
Every guest has a ticket for a short stay, and every ticket has the same closing time written in small print
brief fair
We were hurrying through the crowds at the fair and my father said slow down, we are only visiting, and I have thought about that ever since
Please write a doha in which the world is shown as a festival with a gate and a closing hour, and the guests who dance too hard forget that they are strangers who will soon be out of the gate
Write a doha in which a washerman and a priest both set up at the great fair, the one cleaning clothes and the other blessing them, but both must pack their things and leave when the fair is over
washerman, priest, world's fair
The washerman washes the guests' clothes, the priest blesses their stay, and the fair folds like cloth at dusk
doha with a washerman and a priest, the world is a fair we visit
The washerman and the priest from our village always went to the same fair, and both died the same winter; the fair goes on without them but it is only a fair
Kabir called the world a fair that lasts a few days, in which people meet and part and eat and sleep, and he warned against making a permanent home there, so please write a doha for me in that spirit
fair of few days
The fair is loud with joy and the road home is quiet, and we have all bought a ticket for both
I looked at the empty field after the fair and told my son that is how our whole life is, a few days of lanterns and then the ground; he asked if I was sad
doha about the world being a fair, nothing lasts
There was a heron at the pond behind the fairground and a crow on the fence, and both watched the fair come and go; my mother said it is the same for us
heron, crow, passing fair
doha with a heron and a crow, the world is a fair that closes soon
Write a doha in which a heron and a crow watch the fair from the edge, unmoved, knowing it will close in a few days, and the verse says that the wise watch the world in just that way
The heron stands, the crow calls, and the fair behind them is only a week-old noise
The furnace burns for the fair and cools when the fair is done, and the guests all disperse like smoke
furnace, world is a fair
Please write a doha about a furnace that glows through the nights of a fair, and which is cold by the morning after the last day, so that people see the world as a passing show, not a home
The blacksmith at the festival kept his furnace blazing for three nights, and then it was cold; he told me life is the same, loud and then quiet
doha with a furnace, the world is a fair we visit
The jeweller at the fair sold gold and palanquin ornaments for three days, then packed up; I told him we too are only here for a short season
doha with gold and a palanquin, the world is a fair and we leave
gold, palanquin, passing fair
The palanquin glitters with gold in the fair's procession, but by night the road is empty again

Write a doha in which a palanquin decked with gold passes through the fair, admired by the crowd, though both the gold and the bearers will be gone when the festival ends and the field is returned to the grass
doha with sand and a churn, the world is a fair, we leave
The fairground used to be a sandy field, and the old woman who sold buttermilk from her churn there said that when the fair leaves it returns to being sand; I want a doha for that
sand, churn, passing fair
The sand remembers no footprints, and the churn at the fair rests by evening, for the fair has gone
Please write a doha in which a woman works her churn at a fair on the sand, selling to the crowd, though by morning the sand is smooth and the churn is silent and nobody remembers who stood there
doha about the world being a fair that ends soon
world is a fair
The world is a borrowed room for the soul with its walls painted bright, and the guests come and go before the paint is dry
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying the world is a fair of only a few days, that everyone at it is a visitor, and that the wise leave quietly without clinging to the tents they used
Standing on the empty fairground at dawn, I realised I was a guest here and everything that looked so permanent was only set up for a day
The swan on the lake is a visitor like us, and the winnowing fan at the fair is used only for a few days; I want a doha for the grandfather who taught me this
Write a doha in which a swan floats near the winnowing fan at a fair, and the guests pass by on their short visit, and the swan, knowing the world is brief, drifts on without clinging to the shore
doha with a swan and a winnowing fan, the world is a fair and we leave soon
swan, winnowing fan, passing fair
The swan floats by the winnowing fan at the fair, both guests in a gathering that will not last the week
The tent is pitched at dawn and struck by dusk, and the wise sleep lightly in a place they will leave
temporary stay
My uncle moves city every two years for his work and says that is how he learned that nowhere is permanent; I want a doha about it
doha about us just being guests in this world for a bit
Write a doha in Kabir's voice reminding people that they have come to the fair of the world to see and to learn, not to settle, and that when the time comes they must pick up their bundle and go
well, passing fair
Write a doha where the water well in the middle of the fair is drawn from by hundreds, none of whom own it, all of whom will leave, to show that the world is a fair of passing visitors
The well in the middle of the fair gives drink to all and belongs to none, and the guests depart at dusk
The well at the old fair ground has served visitors for centuries, and the guide told me nobody who came ever stayed; that is life
doha with a well, the world is a fair and we leave soon
The date palm sways and the parrot calls in the middle of the fair, and both are only watching the guests pass
A parrot sat in the date palm all through the fair and then the fair ended and it stayed, watching the field become empty; that is how it feels getting old
date palm, parrot, passing fair
doha with a date palm and a parrot, the world is just a fair that ends
Write a doha in which a parrot sits in a date palm at the fair and calls the names of the passers-by, who will be forgotten when the festival packs up and the palm is left alone
potter and clay, forest, fair
The potter and clay set up at the forest fair, a hundred pots for a hundred guests, and by the end the field is bare
doha with a potter and clay and a forest, the world is a fair we leave soon
Please write a doha in which a potter and clay set up shop at a fair in a forest clearing, sell their wares, and leave, as every guest of the world must leave without keeping the ground
The potter and clay man from the forest set up at our fair each year, and one year he did not come; the fair went on without him, as it will without us
Write a doha in which the forest around the fairground watches the festival come and go every year, as the guests arrive in joy and depart in silence, showing that the world is a short visit
forest, world is a fair
doha with a forest, the world is a short fair that ends
The forest holds the fairground as a cupped hand holds a bird, and in a few days it opens and lets the show go
The fair is set in a clearing in the forest and every year we come for a week and leave it to the trees; I thought, is that what we do with life
I gave my grandson some milk at the fair and told him not to cry when the tents pack up, because that is what life is, and then I started crying myself
Milk is sold at the fair at dawn and the cups are empty by noon, and the fair itself is poured out by night
Write a doha in which a seller of milk at the fair measures out his cups to the crowd, and all the buyers, like the milk, come only briefly and are gone before the day is over
doha with milk in it, the world is a fair that ends soon
milk, world is a fair
The peacock at the zoo spreads its tail for the Sunday visitors and folds it when they leave; I said to my son, that is the world, a Sunday show
doha with a peacock, the world is just a short fair
The peacock spreads for the fair's guests and folds for the dusk, and the fair behind him is folded too
peacock, passing fair
Please write a doha in which a peacock dances at the fair for the visiting crowd, and the verse says that both the peacock's dance and the guests' stay are short, and the wise know when to leave
skeleton, yogi, the fair
doha with a skeleton and a yogi, the world is a short fair
The yogi sits by the skeleton at the edge of the fair, and smiles, for he knows how long the guests stay
A yogi sat at the edge of the fair pointing at a skeleton on a cart and laughing; everyone was uncomfortable, but he said we are all temporary guests here
Write a doha in which a yogi sits at the end of the fair, pointing to a skeleton, telling the guests they are visitors in a short-lived gathering who will all end like this
doha with a cleric and a house, the world is just a fair we visit
My old cleric neighbour said that when you build your house you should build it as if you will leave tomorrow, because this whole world is just a fair
cleric, house, passing fair
The cleric counsels the fairgoers in a borrowed house, and the house, the counsel and the fair all vanish together
Write a doha in which a cleric tells his followers that the house they built is only a tent at the fair, borrowed for a few days, so they should not weep when the festival packs up
doha about a thief at a fair, we are all just visitors here
A thief was caught at the fair with a stolen watch, and the old man said even the thief and the policeman are only visitors on this earth; I want a doha on that
Write a doha in which a thief wanders through the fair stealing from the crowd, though the fair will end in a few days and the stolen goods and the thief will be left behind like everyone else
The thief robs the guests in the fair, and the fair robs the thief of his days, for the stay is short
thief, world is a fair
Write a doha in Kabir's voice saying the world is just a fair, that we came to see the show, and that when the lights go out each guest must go home to where he came from
The great fair of the world is lit for a short hour, and every guest is called by name when it is time to go
I watched a family packing up their tent at the end of the day, tired and happy, and I thought that is us at the end; make me a doha
doha about how this world is a fair and we just stay a few days
world is a fair
My son is sad that the summer festival is over and I told him that all of life is a festival that ends; he asked me to write it down
fair is ending
Please write a doha in simple words saying that the world is a place we visit for a few days, that everyone who comes has a return ticket, and that the wise do not forget the day of departure
doha on us being guests in this world
The festival hums for a few days like a hum in the mouth of the evening, and then the evening closes
doha with a seed, the world is a fair we visit and leave
I sold a seed packet at a tent at the village fair for three days, and on the fourth day it was all gone, even the field; I thought of how our stay is the same
Write a doha in which a seed is sold at a fair to someone who will not stay to see it grow, as a picture of how we plant our lives in a world that is only a short visit
seed, passing fair
A seed is sold at the fair and planted by a guest who will never see it bloom, for the fair is short
lock, passing fair
doha with a lock, the world is a fair we only visit
The lock on the gate of the fair is opened for a few days, and then locked again with nobody left inside
My uncle bought a big lock for his tent at the village fair, and on the last day he sold the lock too; I told him that is what a smart guest does
Write a doha in which a lock is put on a tent at the fair, though the owner will be gone in days and the tent taken apart, to show the world is a short stay that cannot be locked
Write a doha in which the world is a fair run by a great showman who raises the tents in the morning and pulls them down at night, and guests who think it lasts forever are shocked at closing
The great fair of the world is pitched at sunrise and pulled down at sundown, and nobody owns a single peg
doha about this world being a short fair, nothing stays
When the circus left our town my grandfather said that is how the world works, a lot of excitement, a few days, and then an empty ground
brief fair
The sandalwood sold at the fair perfumes the guests for a day, but the fair is a guest too and leaves
sandalwood, passing fair
Please write a doha in which a seller of sandalwood sets up at the world's short fair and fills it with fragrance, though he must leave when the festival ends, taking only the memory of the visit
The old man who sold sandalwood at our festival said he has never stayed more than a week anywhere, and that is how he thinks of life; I want a doha for him
doha with sandalwood, the world is a fair we leave soon
